replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while preserving as much variance as possible. The steps to perform PCA are as follows: first, standardize the data; second, compute the covariance matrix; third, compute the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the covariance matrix; fourth, sort the eigenvectors by their eigenvalues in descending order; fifth, choose the top k eigenvectors, where k is the number of dimensions you want to reduce to; sixth, construct a projection matrix from the top k eigenvectors; seventh, transform the original data using the projection matrix.
